segments: The 58th {OCR?} Jubilee. [p. 283]
Arab Kings.
Mas'ud in Mosul against his brother Sultan Mahmud;
and Amir Zengi was not compliant with him.
And when this Mas'ud gathered an army and engaged with the Sultan his brother,
the Sultan broke him,
and captured him, and put him in irons.
And he gave Mosul to an amir whose name was Bursuqi, together with Jazira, Sinjar, and Nisibis;
and he sent him there.
And at this time, the Greek king of Constantinople sent to Ilghazi son of Artuq, saying:
"Behold, a great multitude of the Franks is coming out from the sea to Syria;
prepare yourself therefore for war against them.
And behold, I am a help to you with thirty thousand [men],
if you have need."
Ilghazi, then, hastened and went and seized the ports,
and they killed a multitude of the Franks,
and the rest turned back to the country of the Franks {OCR?}.
And this was through the evil of the deceitful Greeks.
At this time,
the Armenians of Gargar were secretly raiding and devastating the region of Hisn Ziyad, of Bula, and of Melitene.
And Balak, the Turkish amir, sent word to Michael the Armenian, the lord of Gargar,
that he would give him every year a thousand loads of wheat and three villages in his territory,
if he would restrain his raiders.
And Michael swore many times to Balak,
yet he did not stand by his oaths;
rather, wheat was being sent to him,
while his raiders were burning villages in Hanzit.
Then Balak devised a plan,
and in the month of Shebat, when the mountains were heaped with snow,
he crossed over the ice of the Euphrates to Ghabos.
And on the high mountain which is called Qeryona,
he directed a thousand unladen horses,
and the snow was cleared away.
And the Turkish forces crossed over,
and in one day they reached the front of the monastery of Mor Bar Sawma.
And that very night, they traversed the mountain of Gargar which is called Ista.
And in the morning, he fell upon the miserable territory;
and he plundered it on the second day [of the week? {OCR?}], the beginning of the Later Kanun, the year 1432
[1432 of the Greeks?],
and he swept away and carried off human beings, cattle, and everything, and departed.
And that amir showed great mercy toward the Christian peasants,
and he did not make them into slaves,
but settled them in the region of Hanzit,
and gave them everything that belonged to them.
And he made them swear that they would not return to Gargar,
otherwise, when he invaded a second time, he would spare them no longer.
